lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The v6 readback now surfaces the reminder note, but the reconciled comparison still does not visibly compare the reminder destination even while it says the exact payload matched.
evidence: src/Prototype.tsx:745-750 shows the approval payload fields Destination, Title, Note, When, and Fingerprint.
src/Prototype.tsx:774-777 shows the reconciled comparison as Approved, Observed, and Match, but the Approved and Observed values render only title, note, and time.

src/Prototype.tsx:805-810 shows the verified receipt with destination, title, note, observed time, fact, and operation fingerprint, but the exact-match claim is still carried by the operation line rather than a visible destination comparison.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can see that the reminder text and scheduled instant matched, but cannot directly verify from the reconciled view that the reminder landed in the same destination list that was approved. If destination drifted, the exact-payload wording would overstate certainty.
findings.recommendation: Include destination in the reconciled Approved versus Observed comparison, or narrow the language from exact payload match to the exact fields the UI actually compares. If the fingerprint is intended to cover destination integrity, explain that scope on the surface.
verification: Seed a reconciliation case where destination differs but title, note, time, and fingerprint display would otherwise look plausible, then verify the UI blocks VERIFIED or softens the exact-match claim.
Replay the reconciled state and confirm the visible comparison includes destination, title, note, absolute time, timezone, and operation fingerprint.

strengths: Relative source language is now anchored to visible absolute time and timezone context, including the derivation from "Wednesday" to September 2, 2026, which materially improves auditability of the fact gate (src/Prototype.tsx:88-106, 493, 641-654, 704-709).

Fact confirmation, recruiter correction, revision number, approval binding, and history all stay distinct, preserving the chain from observed quote to confirmed fact to approved effect (src/Prototype.tsx:330-344, 624-668, 744, 952).

Identity remains safely unbound under ambiguity, with no path to attach the historical relationship and an explicit reversible path for saving identity review without changing person or evidence state (src/Prototype.tsx:829-855).

Unknown, failed, insufficient-evidence, and no-action paths remain first-class and truthful, with no optimistic external-success claim before reconciliation and verification (src/Prototype.tsx:759-789, 867-885, 944-953).

The decision dialogs now hide the background from assistive technology and apply focus trapping plus focus restoration, which supports human-authorized review without leaking interaction to the underlying screen during fact or effect approval (src/Prototype.tsx:171-205, 345-349, 696-737).
missing_evidence: This was a code-only blind review with no browser replay, per assignment. I did not directly observe fresh rendered states or console output for the September 4, 2026 freeze.

The code shows the exact-payload and reconciliation contract, but there is no direct proof in this packet that runtime destination readback is actually sourced from an external reminder result rather than mirrored fixture data.
The freeze packet still lists fresh browser screenshots, independent blind specialist packets, and the separate real-human MX-01 comprehension gate as pending.
open_questions: Should the reconciled state be treated as the canonical audit surface for exact payload comparison, or is the receipt intended to hold that responsibility after reconciliation?
If the fingerprint is the true destination-integrity control, where should the UI explain which fields it covers so the recruiter does not over- or under-trust the exact-match claim?
